name: Jahmyr Gibbs
note: Only back averaging 21+ PPR PPG in each of the last two years. David Montgomery's exit to Houston removes the goal-line cap; Detroit's O-line slipping to 13th in PFF run block is the one worry.

name: Bijan Robinson
note: Top-three fantasy RB each of the last two seasons: 1,400+ rushing yards and 60+ catches both years. Genuine 1A/1B with Gibbs.

name: Ja'Marr Chase
note: One of only three receivers projected for 255+ half-PPR points.

name: Puka Nacua
note: Led the league at 23.4 PPR points per game in 2025.

name: Ashton Jeanty
note: Low ankle sprain in an Aug. 23 practice. Fell seven spots to RB10 / No. 16 overall on the 8/25 4for4 update; Week 1 still unclear.

name: Brock Bowers
note: TE1 on most boards - best offense he's played in since entering the league.

name: Trey McBride
note: Wore the crown as 2025's top-scoring tight end. Coin flip with Bowers.

name: Kenneth Walker III
note: Super Bowl MVP in Seattle, then 3 yr / $43.05M to Kansas City with $28.7M guaranteed. Rankers moved him up through camp.

name: Jeremiyah Love
note: No. 3 overall to Arizona, the highest RB taken since Barkley in 2018. Each of the last nine RBs drafted top-12 finished top-12 in fantasy as a rookie.

name: A.J. Brown
note: Traded to New England for a 2028 first and a 2027 fifth. Immediately Drake Maye's No. 1 and reunited with his first head coach.

name: Malik Nabers
note: Had a second procedure to remove a cyclops lesion after his ACL repair. Running routes in camp, but a full Week 1 is unlikely. ADP sliding.

name: Tetairoa McMillan
note: 2025 Offensive Rookie of the Year - 1,014 yards and seven TDs, most among rookie WRs.

name: Emeka Egbuka
case: A rookie star through five weeks before leveling off, which drafters have read as the ceiling rather than the calibration period. Priced as a WR2 for a player with WR1 usage in front of him.

name: Jaylen Waddle
note: Traded to Denver for the No. 30, No. 94 and No. 130 picks. Clear value spike with Bo Nix.

name: Colston Loveland
note: 58-713-6 as a rookie with 90+ receiving yards in each of his final two regular-season games.

name: Tyler Warren
note: 76-817-4 as a rookie - immediately a core piece of the Colts offense.

name: Quinshon Judkins
note: 2025 ended on an ankle injury and fractured fibula. ESPN still has him around RB20.

name: Cam Skattebo
note: Coming back from a major 2025 injury, which is exactly why Tyrone Tracy is a handcuff that matters.

name: Bucky Irving
note: Injury history, Kenny Gainwell's arrival and Sean Tucker vulturing the goal line all push him down from where the talent says he belongs.

name: Josh Allen
note: Only QB to finish top-3 in fantasy PPG in each of the last five seasons, and hasn't missed a start. Every board has him alone in Tier 1.
rushstat: 112 carries (1st), 579 rush yds (1st), 14 rush TD (1st), 36.2 rush yds/g (3rd)
rushnote: The complete profile: he led every quarterback in 2025 in rushing attempts, rushing yards and rushing touchdowns, on a full passing workload. Nobody else is close on all three.

name: Terry McLaurin
note: A quad injury held him to 10 games and a 38-582-3 line. Still Washington's No. 1 if healthy.

name: Rome Odunze
note: The steady one in Chicago while Luther Burden is the explosive one for Caleb Williams.

name: DJ Moore
note: Gives Buffalo the dependable No. 1 they've been missing, and could beat his ADP.

name: Harold Fannin Jr.
note: 72-731-6 as a 21-year-old rookie and a 22% target share, finishing TE6. Njoku's move to the Chargers clears the room entirely.
case: 72-731-6 and a 22% target share as a 21-year-old rookie, good for TE6. Then David Njoku left for the Chargers and handed him the entire room. The Cleveland quarterback situation is the only reason he is not priced higher.

name: David Montgomery
case: Traded to Houston and has already established himself on top of that backfield — RB24 in ADP against RB43 for Woody Marks. The name is familiar enough that nobody is excited, which is the whole point.

name: TreVeyon Henderson
note: Hard to argue past low-end RB2 as long as New England keeps featuring Rhamondre Stevenson.

name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
note: Finally delivered: 88 catches, 928 yards, five TDs in 2025.

name: Carnell Tate
note: A bet on talent plus Cam Ward's year two under Brian Daboll. Tenth in yards per route run and a 68.8% contested-catch rate in college.

name: Stefon Diggs
note: Signed with his hometown team. Led the NFL with a 15.4% catch rate over expected, caught 83.3% of his targets, 2.4 yards per route run.
case: Led the entire NFL in catch rate over expected at 15.4%, caught 83.3% of his targets, and ran 2.4 yards per route — fifth among everyone with 300+ routes. He has risen more than a round twice since signing in Washington and is still a round-10 pick.

name: Jayden Daniels
rushnote: Second among all quarterbacks in rushing yards per game, at a carry rate nobody else sustains. The caveat is sample: elbow, knee and ankle injuries held him to seven games, and his yards per carry fell from 6.0 to 4.8.

name: Lamar Jackson
note: Coming off a subpar, injury-marred year with steep declines in both passing and rushing.
rushstat: The archetype — but 2025 was injury-marred with steep rushing decline
rushnote: The profile that defined the category, entering 2026 off a year with steep declines in both passing and rushing. A new coordinator is the bet, and the badge is on reputation plus history rather than 2025.

name: DK Metcalf
note: Being drafted on name recognition. Right player, wrong offense.

name: Parker Washington
note: From Week 12 on he led Jacksonville at a 25% target share and 14.2 PPR PPG; over the final four games that hit 31% and 18.5.
case: From Week 12 on he led all Jacksonville receivers with a 25% target share and 14.2 PPR points per game. Over the final four games, playoffs included, that became a 31% target share and 18.5 per game on a 26-454-3 line. He is being drafted as though that stretch did not happen.

name: Drake Maye
note: Only Josh Allen outscored him among QBs in 2025 - and now he has A.J. Brown.
rushnote: Arguably the best dual-threat combination in football right now — third among QBs in carries while finishing fourth in the league in passing yards. Both halves, at volume.

name: Kenny Gainwell
case: The exact reason Bucky Irving's price fell is the reason Gainwell has standalone value. Tampa is running a real committee and only one half of it is being drafted.

name: Jonathon Brooks
note: Missed all of 2025 recovering from a second ACL tear. Carolina let Rico Dowdle walk and ignored RB in the draft, which is a real vote of confidence. ADP ~125.
case: A second ACL tear cost him all of 2025, so the market moved on. Carolina did the opposite: they let Rico Dowdle walk and ignored running back entirely in the draft. Dave Canales says he “looks like the guy that I remember.” He climbed nine spots on the 8/25 update and still costs a bench pick for a three-down RB1 outcome.

name: Michael Wilson
note: 2025 was top-heavy - the big games came when Marvin Harrison was out. Fine at WR4 cost, not above it.
case: Jumped nearly eight spots after the first preseason game and is still cheap. The knock is fair — 2025 was top-heavy in the games Marvin Harrison missed. The counter is that Arizona's target tree is still thin behind Harrison.

name: George Kittle
note: Opened camp on PUP with the Achilles he tore in the 2025 playoffs. Reports point to Week 1, but nothing is guaranteed.

name: Jalen Hurts
rushstat: 105 carries (2nd), 421 rush yds (5th), 8 rush TD, 3,224 pass yds
rushnote: Second among quarterbacks in carries and fifth in rushing yards, with the goal-line role attached, on a full 3,200-yard passing season.

name: Jordan Mason
note: Biggest RB mover on the 8/25 update - up 16 spots to RB36.

name: Jayden Reed
case: Green Bay's slot receiver in a room where the market is busy arguing about Golden and Watson. Availability is the real question, not talent.

name: Kyle Monangai
note: Forced his way into a committee as a seventh-round rookie: 41% of Chicago's snaps, 4.6 YPC on 169 carries.

name: Xavier Worthy
note: Kansas City moved on from Marquise Brown and Smith-Schuster and added only a fifth-rounder. They still trust him as a starter.
case: Kansas City moved on from Marquise Brown and Smith-Schuster and replaced them with a fifth-round rookie. That is a roster telling you who it trusts. Third year, fastest man out of the 2024 class, and the last starter standing.

name: Joe Burrow
note: Held around QB4 despite the ceiling, purely on durability.

name: Blake Corum
note: The consensus No. 1 backup RB. 782 scrimmage yards and six TDs in year two, with the Rams' split projected near 60/40.

name: Deebo Samuel
note: Back in Shanahan's system and three years younger than Mike Evans. Unsexy, but he'll start and score.

name: Josh Downs
note: Moving up from the slot to Indy's No. 2, working underneath opposite Tyler Warren.
case: Moving out of the slot into Indianapolis's No. 2 job. That makes him Daniel Jones' primary underneath target working opposite Tyler Warren, which is a volume role at a WR4 price.

name: Travis Kelce
note: Back at 37 on a one-year deal. 76-851 on 108 targets last year - volume intact, but 13 total TDs across three seasons is a career low.

name: Jaxson Dart
rushstat: 81 carries (5th), 455 rush yds (3rd), 9 rush TD, 35.0 rush yds/g (4th) — but only 2,272 pass yds
rushnote: Top-five in carries and third in rushing yards with nine rushing scores in 12 starts. The passing half is not there: 2,272 yards in 14 games, and the Giants are expected to be run-first again. Elite runner, not yet a dual threat.

name: Jalen Nailor
note: Vegas's big offseason signing and their camp WR1, though Brock Bowers will lead that team in receiving.
case: Las Vegas's big offseason signing and their camp WR1. Brock Bowers will lead that team in receiving, but Nailor is the receiver to own there and he costs a WR5 pick.

name: Tyrone Tracy Jr.
note: Averaged 16.9 touches and 12.9 PPR points across the 10 games Skattebo wasn't the clear lead back.
case: Averaged 16.9 touches and 12.9 PPR points across the 10 games Cam Skattebo was not the clear lead back. Skattebo is coming back from a major injury. This is the cheapest handcuff with a starter's outcome attached.

name: Dalton Kincaid
note: Fantasy's biggest TE wild card. An efficiency darling on a 38% snap share while Buffalo managed a knee issue.

name: Rashid Shaheed
note: Was breaking out in New Orleans before the trade to Seattle. Should be Darnold's No. 2 and the deep threat opposite JSN.
case: Was breaking out in New Orleans before the midseason trade to Seattle. Now he is Sam Darnold's No. 2 and the deep threat working opposite Smith-Njigba, and he is being drafted like a change-of-pace piece.

name: T.J. Hockenson
note: A 16% target share and 51-438-3, then a shoulder injury. Kyler Murray should help, but show me first.

name: Adonai Mitchell
note: Set to start opposite Garrett Wilson for a team that will play from behind a lot. A popular late-round favorite.
case: Set to start opposite Garrett Wilson for a team that will be playing from behind most weeks. Third-year receivers with a defined starting job and negative game script are how late-round WR rooms get won.

name: Tank Bigsby
note: The Saquon handcuff, full stop.
case: Not a sleeper if Saquon plays 17 games. The full Barkley workload is one of maybe three handcuff outcomes in football that wins a league outright.

name: Mason Taylor
case: Led the Jets in both catches and targets as a rookie despite playing 13 games. Aaron Glenn named him a breakout candidate in mid-August, which is usually a coach telling you the target share is going up.

name: KC Concepcion
note: 24th overall to Cleveland under new HC Todd Monken. Roughly 100 targets would have been a top-30 fantasy WR season last year.

name: Travis Hunter
note: Target hierarchy in Jacksonville is genuinely unsettled with Brian Thomas Jr. healthy. Priced as a WR5 lottery ticket.

name: Nick Singleton
case: One of the best late stashes on the board — the talent and the opening to become a difference-maker in exactly the weeks the fantasy playoffs happen.

name: Rashod Bateman
case: Five years of waiting has trained everyone to stop looking. He is still the perimeter starter on an offense that scores, and the cost is now nothing.

name: Jonah Coleman
case: Sits behind J.K. Dobbins and R.J. Harvey in Denver, and Dobbins' health is a perpetual red flag. Touchdown-dependent as an RB3, but he could lead that team in rushing scores.

name: De'Zhaun Stribling
note: Rookie second-rounder, sixth WR off the board. Ricky Pearsall's season-ending knee surgery opened the door and Stribling has been San Francisco's best camp receiver.
case: The single biggest riser on the board over the last week, and it still may not be enough. Ricky Pearsall's season-ending knee surgery cleared the room and Stribling — a second-round rookie, sixth receiver drafted — has been San Francisco's best camp receiver.

name: David Njoku
note: Signed with the Chargers after Fannin pushed him down Cleveland's chart.

name: Caleb Williams
note: Tied for eighth among QBs in fantasy points per game last season.
rushstat: 77 carries, 388 rush yds, 3 rush TD, 3,942 pass yds (7th)
rushnote: 77 carries and 388 yards on the ground with the seventh-most passing yards in the league. A tier below the top on rushing volume, but both halves are real.

name: Jayden Higgins
note: Conflicting August reporting - one outlet removed him for a torn ACL, others had him as C.J. Stroud's clear No. 2. Verify status before you draft him.

name: Kyler Murray
note: Released by Arizona, signed a one-year deal in Minnesota.

name: Jalen Coker
case: An undrafted free agent who built a genuine connection with Bryce Young. Large frame, hard worker, and a third-year breakout is live if Carolina's passing game takes any step at all.

name: Emmett Johnson
case: The rookie behind Kenneth Walker III in an offense that just paid $43M for its backfield. Handcuff logic, zero cost.

name: Isaac TeSlaa
case: Locked in as Detroit's No. 3 and a genuine red-zone body on one of the league's best offenses. One step forward makes him relevant.

name: Tyler Shough
case: Strong down the stretch as a rookie, and New Orleans spent the offseason propping the offense up around him — Travis Etienne in, Jordyn Tyson drafted eighth overall. Projection models keep flagging him as a steal.

name: Oronde Gadsden II
note: Year-two path got crowded fast - the Chargers added both David Njoku and Charlie Kolar.

name: Cyrus Allen
case: A fifth-round rookie turning heads in Kansas City camp with a path to real Patrick Mahomes targets. There is no cost to being wrong here.

name: Justin Herbert
rushstat: 83 carries (4th), 498 rush yds (2nd), 31.1 rush yds/g (5th), 3,727 pass yds (9th)
rushnote: Top-five in all three rushing categories and ninth in the league in passing yards. On the raw numbers this is a genuine dual threat, and he is the cheapest one on the board.

name: Patrick Mahomes
note: Coming off December knee surgery. Says the knee feels great and hasn't missed a camp practice, but it has been years since he was a fantasy superstar.
rushstat: 422 rush yds (4th), 30.1 rush yds/start, full passing workload
rushnote: Fourth among quarterbacks in rushing yards, which is more than the reputation carries. Price in the December knee surgery.

name: Gunnar Helm
case: As a rookie he posted a 22.4% target-per-route-run rate and 1.45 yards per route, both better than Chig Okonkwo, on an 80% catch rate. Cam Ward gets more comfortable in year two and Helm becomes the security blanket. You can take him with your last pick.

name: Baker Mayfield
case: Routinely available in the 12th or 13th round. If you punt quarterback entirely, this is where you land and it is a fine place to land.

name: Terrance Ferguson
case: The buzziest name in Rams camp all summer, getting extended first-team reps from Sean McVay. Only 25 targets as a rookie but 21 yards per catch, and the Rams are visibly expanding his route tree.

name: Greg Dulcich
case: In position to step forward as a second primary target in Miami. A late-round tight end with a defined role beats a late-round tight end without one.

name: Malik Willis
rushstat: 60.0 rush yds/start — highest rate of any QB — on a small starting sample
rushnote: The highest rushing rate at the position by a distance, but on limited starts and without the passing volume to pair with it. Great rushing floor, thin everything else.

name: Cam Ward
note: Real QB2 upside after Tennessee added Carnell Tate and put Brian Daboll in charge of the offense.

name: Aaron Rodgers
note: Locked in as Pittsburgh's QB1 - their first repeat Week 1 starter since 2020-21.

name: Deshaun Watson
note: Named Cleveland's Week 1 starter by Todd Monken - a situation worth re-checking on draft day.

name: Kirk Cousins
note: The bridge in Las Vegas ahead of No. 1 overall pick Fernando Mendoza.

name: Tua Tagovailoa
note: In an unresolved Atlanta competition with Michael Penix Jr.

name: Brandon Aubrey
note: Top-projected kicker at roughly 116 half-PPR points.

name: Ka'imi Fairbairn
note: 44-of-48 on field goals in 15 games, tying the single-season record.
